root_cause.text: The `__smc_setsockopt()` function in the SMC network subsystem holds the socket lock while executing `copy_from_sockptr()` on user-provided data, allowing an attacker to trigger a page fault that sleeps while the lock is held, resulting in a denial of service.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows `copy_from_sockptr` moved before `lock_sock(sk)`, and the CVE description states "The function __smc_setsockopt() calls copy_from_sockptr() while holding lock_sock(sk)."

Author: Ursula Braun <ubraun@linux.ibm.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 26 17:18:21 2018 +0200

    net/smc: handle sockopts forcing fallback
    
    Several TCP sockopts do not work for SMC. One example are the
    TCP_FASTOPEN sockopts, since SMC-connection setup is based on the TCP
    three-way-handshake.
    If the SMC socket is still in state SMC_INIT, such sockopts trigger
    fallback to TCP. Otherwise an error is returned.
    
    Signed-off-by: Urs
